title: Teriyaki Chicken Donburi
subtitle: Glazed chicken over steamed rice
description: Glazed chicken over steamed rice. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Teriyaki Chicken Donburi in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Steam rice
steps.instruction: Cook short-grain rice 1:1.25 with water; keep covered and warm. Plan about 18 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Sear chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Pat chicken thighs dry; sear in oiled skillet over medium-high 5 minutes skin-side down until golden. Flip; cook 4 more minutes. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and steam broccoli
steps.instruction: Add teriyaki sauce to the pan; simmer 3–4 minutes until chicken reads 165°F and sauce thickens to a glaze. Steam broccoli 4 minutes until bright green.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Teriyaki Chicken Donburi onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Build donburi bowls
steps.instruction: Mound rice in bowls, slice glazed chicken over top, add broccoli, sesame seeds, and green onions. Teriyaki Chicken Donburi should glisten — thin with a splash of sauce if it tightens too much.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Teriyaki Chicken Donburi — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Set rice or grain in the first pan, main in the second, crunchy toppings last so textures stay distinct.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end of the line.
Line up Teriyaki Chicken Donburi on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Glazed chicken over steamed rice. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Teriyaki Chicken Donburi runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
